title: "Welcome development" as inquest called in police-involving fatal shooting of teen
article: The leader of the Southern Chiefs Organization (SCO) is pleased that Manitoba's Chief Medical Examiner has ordered an inquest into the death of 16-year-old Eishia Hudson, who was shot and killed by a Winnipeg Police officer last April.

"This is a welcome development after the Independent Investigation Unit (IIU) did not lay criminal charges against the officer who shot and killed Eishia last year," said Grand Chief Jerry Daniels in a statement. "We are hopeful that this inquest will provide us with the answers we have been seeking since this tragic event took place."
Manitoba's Chief Medical Examiner Dr. John K. Younes called an inquest into the death, it was announced Friday.

"SCO and Eishia's family want this process to be thorough, unbiased and comprehensive," said Daniels. "To honour Eishia's memory we need to do everything we can to make sure she did not die in vain, and that we can bring an end to deaths of our people at the hands of colonial police forces."
The incident took place on April 8, 2020, following an alleged theft at a Liquor Mart in Sage Creek which led to a police pursuit of a stolen vehicle.

In a statement Friday from the provincial government, the pursuit continued in the Sage Creek area and onto Lagimodiere Blvd. at high rates of speed. Shortly after the stolen vehicle crossed the median at Lagimodiere Blvd. and Fermor Avenue where it was stopped by several WPS vehicles. While apprehending the five occupants, a WPS officer discharged his firearm striking Hudson, the driver. She was taken to Health Sciences Centre where she was pronounced dead.

The medical examiner's office was notified and an autopsy was performed with the cause of death determined to be gunshot wound to the torso. The manner of death was determined to be homicide, the medical examiner's office said.

In late January, the IIU released its findings following an investigation into the incident. After consulting with the Manitoba Prosecution Services, it was determined that no criminal charges would be laid against the officer.
Information as to the date, time and location of the inquest will be determined by the Chief Judge of the Provincial Court of Manitoba and released at a later date.
